title: First Grey Avenue
descriptionHtml:
GREY MELANCHOLY AVENUE IS A SCREEN PRINT PAINSTAKINGLY CREATED WITH ELEVEN SHADES OF GREY TO CREATE THE ILLUSION OF A FOG-SHROUDED DISTANCE AS YOU LOOK DOWN THE AVENUE. THE DRAWING FROM WHICH THIS PRINT IS TAKEN IS THE ILLUSTRATION FOR THE SECTION ENTITLED ‘MELANCHOLY’ IN STANLEY DONWOOD’S COLLECTION ‘HUMOR’, PUBLISHED IN NOVEMBER BY FABER & FABER. THE PRINT IS HAND PRINTED ON TO 300GSM SOMERSET VELVET PAPER MADE AT ST CUTHBERT’S MILL IN WELLS, SOMERSET, AND LIMITED TO AN EDITION OF ONLY 23 PRINTS.

title: Upturn Blue
descriptionHtml:
THIS IS A REWORKING OF A SMALLER PRINT CALLED ‘UPTURN’ PRODUCED FOR (AND WAS ONLY AVAILABLE AT) CHAPTER ARTS CENTRE IN CARDIFF. HERE’S WHAT I WROTE ABOUT IT:
“DESPITE THE ONGOING ECONOMIC DISASTERS ENGENDERED BY THE MENDACIOUS MOVEMENTS OF THE FINANCE INDUSTRY, WE ARE INFORMED THAT THE APPROPRIATION BY THE WEALTHY OF EVER MORE OF THE WORLD'S RESOURCES IS 'WORKING' AND WILL LEAD US TO A SHINING 'RECOVERY'. TO CELEBRATE THIS UPTURN I PRESENT A SMALL PRINT OF A DIFFERENT KIND OF UPTURN. AN UPTURNED CAR. COMPLETE WITH A REFUGEE.”
THIS IS A THREE-COLOUR SCREEN PRINT, HAND PRINTED ON TO 300GSM SOMERSET VELVET PAPER.

EDITION SIZE:77

PRINT SIZE:375MM X 290MM APPROX
PAPER SIZE:490MM X 375MM

title: Treasure Island Sunset blue version and red version
descriptionHtml:
THIS SCREEN PRINT IS ADAPTED FROM A LINOCUT I DID FOR THE COVER OF RL STEVENSON’S ‘TREASURE ISLAND’, COMMISSIONED FOR A NEW PUBLICATION OF STEVENSON’S 1883 NOVEL. I SPENT A WHILE FIGURING OUT HOW TO DO IT, AND PERHAPS INFLUENCED BY THE JAPANESE ARTIST HOKUSAI, EVENTUALLY SETTLED ON HUGE STYLISED WAVES AS A FOREGROUND AND A TINY, EASILY-MISSED ISLAND UNDER A STORMY SKY. THE PICTURE HAS BEEN AVAILABLE PREVIOUSLY AS A VERY SMALL, ONE COLOUR LETTERPRESS PRINT IN AN OPEN EDITION; THIS MUCH LARGER VERSION HAS BEEN SCREEN PRINTED IN THREE COLOURS, AND IS HAND PRINTED ON TO 300GSM SOMERSET VELVET PAPER.

title: Aeratus Llyn
descriptionHtml:
This trio of prints were made to enquire into the difficulty of reaching somewhere far away on a journey made on foot. Somewhere quiet where all the clamour is forgotten and the loudest shouting is from the wind.

This eight-layer screen print is called 'Aeratus Llyn; aeratus being the Latin for bronze and llyn being a Welsh word used to describe a lake.

This print was made by mixing bronze powder from L.Cornelissen & Son in London with varnish, and to create the effect of distance, different layers of black ink are interspersed with the bronze varnish.  The original drawings were made with a brush and ink on layers of tracing paper.

A hand-pulled screen print on Fabriano Rosapina Bianco paper. Signed and numbered by Stanley Donwood and blind-embossed with the Slowly Downward Manufactory Stamp.

Paper size: 420mm x 290mm 
Print size: 320mm x 210mm 
Paper weight : 285gsm
From an edition of 145 prints

title: Argentum Sgúrr
descriptionHtml:
This trio of prints were made to enquire into the difficulty of reaching somewhere far away on a journey made on foot. Somewhere quiet where all the clamour is forgotten and the loudest shouting is from the wind.

This eight-layer screen print is called 'Argentum Sgúrr'; argentum being the latin for silver and sgúrr being a Gaelic word used to describe a peak.

This print was made by mixing silver powder from L.Cornelissen & Son in London with varnish, and to create the effect of distance, different layers of blue ink are interspersed with the silver varnish.  The original drawings were made with a brush and ink on layers of tracing paper.

A hand-pulled screen print on Fabriano Rosapina Bianco paper. Signed and numbered by Stanley Donwood and blind-embossed with the Slowly Downward Manufactory Stamp.

Paper size : 420mm x 290mm (16.5" x 11.5")
Print size : 320mm x 210mm (12.5" x 8.25")
Paper weight : 285gsm
From an edition of 130 prints

title: Flood Barrier
descriptionHtml:
Taken from the series 'London Views', which is a panorama of London being destroyed by fire and flood carved in lino in a quasi-Mediaeval style. The work was made in 2006, thirteen years ago, and once more seems deeply apposite, as the United Kingdom sets about an incomprehensible process of self-immolation.  The black is very shiny and the white is just about perceptible !

Two colour hand-pulled screen print.
Edition of 100.
Print size 340mm x 520mm (approx).
Paper size 420mm x 640mm.
Numbered and signed by the artist.
Blind-embossed with the Slowly Downward Manufactory seal.
